articles.title: Draft NUREG: Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities
articles.summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing for public comment a draft report entitled, NUREG-1307, Revision 21, "Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities." This report, which is revised periodically, explains the formula acceptable to the NRC for determining the minimum decommissioning fund requirements for nuclear power reactor licensees, as required by NRC regulations. Specifically, this report provides the adjustment factor and updates the values for the labor, energy, and waste burial escalation factors of the minimum formula.

Seville Port Authority’s board approved the selection of AG Seville Shipyard on October 20, allowing the company to retain its position at the former Astilleros del Guadalquivir facilities. The operator’s existing concession expires in December.The new concession will cover approximately 22,000 sq m of port land and infrastructure, including the dry dock, the southern section of the Muelle de Armamento and a disused slipway. The concession can run for up to 25 years, although final administrative approval is still required before the new agreement becomes effective. AG Seville Shipyard faced competition for the facilities from Spanish maritime group Boluda, which had also expressed interest in taking over the site. The successful operator has controlled part of the former Seville shipyard since 2017, developing ship repair and maintenance operations at facilities that had suffered years of decline following the collapse of the former public shipyard. The company plans to invest approximately €10m ($11.2m) in modernisation and expansion projects under the new concession. articles.content: Iraqi Line returns to Gulf container trade after 50 years - Splash247 ICTSI Iraq’s national shipping line is returning to scheduled container services in the Gulf after more than half a century, as the country seeks to rebuild maritime connections disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis. According to Alphaliner, Iraqi Maritime Line is deploying the 902 teu Basrah on an eight-day shuttle linking Jebel Ali in Dubai with Umm Qasr, Iraq’s principal container gateway. The first sailing was scheduled to depart Jebel Ali yesterday, arriving in Umm Qasr two days later. Iraq’s transport ministry has described the initiative as the national carrier’s first regular Gulf operation since the mid-1960s. The relaunch comes as Iraqi container supply chains have been radically reshaped since the Hormuz shipping crisis erupted at the end of February. Growing volumes have been diverted to Jordan’s Red Sea port of Aqaba before travelling overland into Iraq through the Trebil border crossing. According to the Jordan Shipping Association, Aqaba handled 37,182 Iraq-bound transit containers during the first seven months of 2026, compared with just 3,599 during the corresponding period last year, a 933% increase. Maersk has introduced landbridge services connecting Aqaba with Iraq, while CMA CGM has offered alternative routings through Aqaba for southern Iraq and Turkey’s Mersin for northern destinations. According to Xclusiv Shipbrokers, the New York-listed owner has lined up two ships at the CSSC-controlled yard, priced at around $109m each, with delivery scheduled for 2029. Neither Danaos nor the shipbuilder has publicly confirmed the deal. If finalised, it would mark the Greek owner’s first newbuilding contract at Waigaoqiao. Danaos has been a regular customer of Chinese shipyards in recent years, spreading orders across several builders as it renews and expands its containership fleet. The company already has seven 9,200 teu vessels under construction at other Chinese yards under contracts placed in 2024, with deliveries scheduled between 2027 and 2028. Its more recent investments include six 1,800 teu feeder vessels booked in November last year for delivery through 2029, followed by four 5,300 teu ships at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong, disclosed in February. articles.content: Gestion Maritime makes ultramax debut with China order - Splash247 Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering Monaco-based shipowner Gestion Maritime is moving into the ultramax segment with an order for three 64,000 dwt bulk carriers at China’s Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering. The Danilo Fumarola-led company has booked the trio for delivery between late 2028 and early 2029, expanding beyond its traditional panamax and kamsarmax fleet. The vessels are costing in the low $30m range apiece, putting the overall investment at more than $90m. Gestion Maritime currently operates six panamax and kamsarmax bulkers and has recently trimmed its fleet through asset sales. The latest investment will bring smaller and more modern tonnage into a portfolio built largely around Japanese- and South Korean-built ships. The company, whose roots date back to 1908 and the Corrado shipping family, has traditionally pursued an asset trading strategy, buying ships when values ease and disposing of tonnage during stronger markets. In 2019, it exited the product tanker sector by selling two 2015-built MR tankers to Hafnia interests for $31m each, returning its focus to dry bulk. The newbuilding deal adds another international owner to Nantong Xiangyu’s growing customer base. The Chinese shipbuilder marked the delivery of its 100th ultramax bulker in July and has continued to attract orders for the 63,500 to 64,000 dwt segment. articles.content: Aker BP and Höegh Evi secure EU funding for North Sea CO2 storage project - Splash247 Aker BP Norwegian offshore producer Aker BP and maritime infrastructure specialist Höegh Evi have secured €223m ($260m) from the European Union Innovation Fund for their Atlas carbon transport and storage project in the North Sea. The project aims to establish a large-scale carbon capture and storage (CCS) network that links industrial emitters across Europe to permanent storage facilities on the Norwegian continental shelf through a combination of collection hubs, specialised CO2 carriers, and subsea injection infrastructure. Atlas has an initial design capacity of 6m tonnes of CO2 annually, with potential to expand beyond 10m tonnes as the European carbon storage market develops. Under the proposed system, the project would aggregate captured CO2 at regional export hubs near industrial clusters before transporting it aboard dedicated low-pressure carriers to the offshore storage site. CO2 would be injected directly through subsea infrastructure into a saline aquifer more than 2,000 m below the seabed, removing the need for extensive onshore pipeline networks. The project was recognised as an EU Project of Mutual Interest in April 2026, acknowledging its potential to provide cross-border carbon transport and storage infrastructure. articles.title: Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting
articles.summary:
From a $12 million cargo theft scheme to fraudulent shipment diversions, recent cases reveal a recurring weakness. The question is whether your team knows how to recognize it before freight moves.
The post Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: Millions in stolen freight reveal a weakness criminals keep exploiting - FreightWaves Recent freight fraud investigations have exposed millions of dollars in cargo losses across the United States. Federal prosecutors recently charged a driver in an alleged $12 million cargo theft conspiracy involving established trucking companies. A California trucking owner pleaded guilty in a separate $2.1 million identity theft case. Another investigation uncovered a nationwide cargo theft ring that purchased existing motor carriers to secure freight. Although these investigations involve different suspects, several reveal the same vulnerability within freight transportation. Criminals exploit legitimate business identities, established operating authorities, and trusted communications to gain control of shipments. Their tactics can make fraudulent transactions appear legitimate during routine carrier verification. The question is whether employees know what to verify before releasing freight. Established authority does not establish identity Federal prosecutors recently charged Nursulton Khaydarov in connection with an alleged cargo theft conspiracy exceeding $12 million. Investigators identified at least 24 shipments involving trucking companies that suspects allegedly purchased or controlled. The 18th Pyongyang Autumn International Trade Fair opened at the Central Youth Hall in Pyongyang on Monday, under the theme of "Common development and prosperity," the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. More than 130 companies from North Korea, China, Mongolia, Bangladesh and Thailand are showcasing over 10,000 products from electronics products and machinery to medicines, building materials and foodstuffs, according to the report. External Economic Relations Minister Yun Jong-ho attended the opening ceremony, alongside officials and exhibitors. In his opening speech, Yun vowed to "expand external economic relations" with countries and regions around the world on the principle of "complete equality and reciprocity," the report said. North Korea holds trade fairs each spring and fall to attract foreign investment and boost trade amid international sanctions. articles.content: Zijin Mining orders bulker pair for African mineral trade - Splash247 Xinneng Shipbuilding Chinese mining giant Zijin Mining has returned to Shandong Xinneng Shipbuilding for two 3,000 dwt bulk carriers, expanding its dedicated mineral transport operation on Lake Tanganyika in eastern Africa. The latest contract follows an earlier order for four 2,000 dwt vessels at the same Chinese yard, which are now operating on the lake between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania. The new ships will be 50% larger than their predecessors, adding a combined 6,000 dwt to Zijin’s lake transport capacity. Contract value and delivery dates have not been disclosed. The investment forms part of Zijin’s efforts to establish an alternative export corridor for minerals from its operations in the DRC. The group’s existing shipping operation links Congolese cargoes with Kigoma in Tanzania, from where they can move towards the country’s Indian Ocean export infrastructure. Zijin’s first four lake bulkers were built through an arrangement that saw hull sections manufactured in China and assembled in Tanzania, overcoming the logistical challenges of building vessels for an African inland waterway. The company established the route to support its growing mining interests in central Africa and reduce dependence on existing overland transport connections. articles.content: US moves to extend China ship fee truce into 2027 - Splash247 Port of Long Beach The United States is looking to extend its suspension of additional port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold until January 9, 2027, while trade negotiations with Beijing continue. The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) has opened a public consultation on a proposal to prolong the suspension from November 10, when the current arrangement expires. Under the proposed extension, operators would continue to be exempt from the additional maritime transport charges introduced under Washington’s Section 301 investigation into China’s dominance of shipping, logistics and shipbuilding. The proposal would also maintain the suspension of separate duties on certain cargo-handling equipment. The US initially introduced the vessel charges in October 2025, targeting Chinese-owned and operated ships, Chinese-built tonnage operated by non-Chinese companies and certain foreign-built vehicle carriers. The measures prompted widespread changes to fleet deployment plans, with owners and operators looking to limit their exposure to the additional costs. Washington and Beijing subsequently agreed to suspend their respective maritime charges for one year as part of a broader trade agreement, with the American suspension taking effect on November 10, 2025. articles.content: Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Reuters Total Views: 61 October 22, 2026 ATHENS, Oct 22 (Reuters) – The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism. The statement comes after the US Treasury Department said on Wednesday it imposed sanctions on Karnakis & Karnakis, a law firm based in Greece and Panama, saying it had for years provided legal assistance to Iranian shipping networks. The Treasury also said that the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued an administrative subpoena to advance an investigation into a Greek bank, which it did not name. The Greek finance ministry said it had taken note of the US Treasury statement, adding that “all available information is being evaluated, and appropriate measures are being taken in accordance with established procedures and applicable national, EU, and international law.” (Reporting by Angeliki Koutantou; Editing by Aidan Lewis) (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026. OK By Oh Seok-min SEOUL, Oct. 22 (Yonhap) -- Cuba is seeking to deepen economic ties with South Korea as it has been grappling with the economic and energy crises exacerbated by decadeslong U.S. sanctions on Havana, the Cuban ambassador to Seoul has said. General Assembly on Cuba's annual resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo. (Yonhap) "There has been a constant trickle of new measures and sanctions that affect both the public and private sectors," Monzon said. The ambassador said intensified U.S. sanctions have had far-reaching effects on Cuba's trade, fuel supplies and public services, including healthcare. "If not the worst, it's at least one of the worst situations we've been through," he said. Cuba has submitted an annual resolution against the U.S. embargo since 1992, and this year will be no exception, with a vote scheduled for Oct. 27-28. "

articles.content: China's green corridor push hits commercial reality check - Splash247 CMB.TECH China has emerged as a major player in the global green shipping corridor movement, with at least 21 initiatives linked to the country, although most remain in their early stages and only one has progressed towards commercial operation, according to a new report from the Global Maritime Forum. The study, released during the organisation’s annual summit in Shanghai, shows that China accounts for nearly a fifth of the world’s green shipping corridor initiatives, having added ten new projects in 2025 alone. However, of the 21 initiatives identified by the end of June this year, 12 were still at the initiation stage, five were exploring feasibility, three had reached preparation and just one had entered the realisation phase. The most advanced is the Australia-East Asia Iron Ore corridor, involving the deployment of ammonia-powered bulk carriers between Australia’s Pilbara region and China. The report also highlights how much of the sector’s future fuel supply is increasingly concentrated in China. The country accounts for around 80% of global green methanol production capacity that has passed final investment decision and more than 40% of comparable green ammonia capacity. articles.content: VLCC delivery wave set to reach levels not seen since the 1970s - Splash247 Hengli Group The VLCC sector is heading for its biggest delivery wave in half a century, with more than 100 new supertankers scheduled to enter service annually in both 2028 and 2029, according to Hartland Shipping Services. The scale recalls the supertanker boom of the 1970s. BIMCO’s historical figures put the all-time record at 116 VLCCs delivered in 1974. Since then, even the 68 deliveries recorded in 2019 represented a four-decade high. The historical precedent is worth noting. A wave of tankers ordered during the early 1970s boom arrived just as the 1973 oil shock devastated demand. Between 1974 and 1975, global oil trade plunged 23% while tanker capacity grew nearly 16%, according to UNCTAD. Freight rates collapsed. The reopening of the Suez Canal in 1975 further shortened voyages. By year-end, 573 tankers representing 47.8m dwt were laid up, according to INTERTANKO. Owners faced financial ruin, newbuildings went straight into lay-up and the industry endured a prolonged depression. Hartland now counts 319 VLCCs on order, equivalent to 34% of the existing fleet, rising to 42% when sanctioned ships are excluded. Yet just 20 are scheduled for delivery over the next six months. Only six VLCCs delivered last year and just one in 2024. This could be an upcoming supply disaster Of the current orderbook, 138 ships are not due until 2029 or later. articles.content: Trader Alkagesta enters shipowning with Turkish bunker fleet takeover - Splash247 Energy Petrol Malta-based commodities trader Alkagesta is entering shipowning through the acquisition of Turkish marine fuel supplier Energy Petrol, taking over an eight-vessel bunker fleet as it expands its physical fuel distribution business. The Orkhan Rustamov-led company confirmed on October 22 that it had agreed to acquire the Istanbul-based supplier in a transaction already approved by Türkiye’s competition authority. Financial terms have not been disclosed, and Energy Petrol is expected to continue operating independently. The deal marks Alkagesta’s first investment in owned vessels, moving the group beyond fuel trading and chartered shipping into direct physical distribution. Energy Petrol, established in 1997 by Mustafa and Yeşim Muhtaroğlu, is an established bunker supplier in the Turkish Straits region. The company operates bunker tankers supplying marine gasoil and fuel oil, with its fleet including the 3,659 dwt Deniz M, the 2,818 dwt Energy K and smaller vessels serving the Istanbul market. Energy Petrol’s website lists a wider historical fleet, although the companies have not identified which eight vessels are included in the transaction. Alkagesta estimates that it already supplies approximately 40% of Turkey’s annual 2.5m-tonne marine fuel market and around 75% of Malta’s bunkering market. articles.content: New Drewry data shows import demand boosting trans-Pacific rates - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Drewry’s World Container Index rose 2% to $4,585 per 40-foot container, supported by higher rates on trans-Pacific and Asia-Europe routes as strong U.S. import demand and carrier capacity cuts bolstered pricing. Shanghai-to-Los Angeles rates increased 2% to $8,007 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-New York rates edged up 1% to $10,166. Drewry expects trans-Pacific rates to remain stable next week, with U.S. import demand continuing to support the market despite an increase in available capacity. Carriers have announced only two blank sailings on the trans-Pacific for next week, down from six this week, according to figures from Drewry’s Container Capacity Insight. The service tracks scheduled and canceled sailings, effective capacity and port congestion across major trade lanes. Rates from Shanghai to Rotterdam rose 3% to $3,632 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-Genoa rates increased 5% to $4,152. Unlike the trans-Pacific, the Asia-Europe trade faces more sailing cancellations next week. Carriers have announced eight blank sailings, up from two this week, tightening available capacity as they seek to put upward pressure on freight rates. articles.content: Workforce gaps keep supply chain AI stuck in pilot mode - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Freight technology vendors are selling AI agents that can benchmark rates and award freight under rules a customer sets. A new survey finds most supply chain organizations still limit AI to generating insights, and the first obstacle the research names is their own workforce. The Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute (DSCI) released The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration on Oct. 14. Of the supply chain professionals surveyed, 83% said their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively. The 17% who described their workforce as ready reported a 71% AI project success rate. Everyone else reported 28%, and about 64% of that group is still in the pilot or planning stage. Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM, said most AI sessions at supply chain conferences run through the same agenda: the challenges, the implementation, and the benefits. Every one of them ends with a reminder not to forget about the people, he said. “It’s interesting because from our perspective that’s where you ought to start the conversation,” Eshkenazi told FreightWaves. AI mostly stays in planning The report scored AI adoption across 13 core supply chain functions on a scale from 1, meaning no AI use, to 5, meaning autonomous execution without human review. articles.content: Icon Energy faces shareholder revolt over dilution - Splash247 Icon Energy Nasdaq-listed Greek dry bulk owner Icon Energy is facing pressure from a significant shareholder to overhaul its capital structure and board, following accusations that repeated equity issuances have heavily diluted ordinary investors. Canada’s Hampton Financial, which holds 325,000 Icon shares representing approximately 9% of the company, has disclosed a letter sent to Icon’s management demanding changes to its preferred shares, dividend arrangements and corporate governance. Hampton, led by chairman and chief executive Peter Deeb, claims Icon has raised approximately $25m through common share issuances since its 2024 flotation, while ordinary shareholders have suffered substantial losses. The Canadian investment firm has also questioned the treatment of preferred shares held by Icon’s controlling shareholder and chief executive, Ismini Panagiotidi. Hampton is proposing that Icon exchange its outstanding Series A preferred shares for a new instrument with a $20m face value, a fixed 6% cash dividend and conversion rights priced at $5 per ordinary share. It also wants a one-for-one share dividend for existing ordinary shareholders and the appointment of a Hampton-nominated director. The investor argues that these measures would address dilution concerns while preserving Panagiotidi’s control of the business. articles.content: Laskaridis linked to $312m newcastlemax order in China - Splash247 Changhong International Greek shipowner Panos Laskaridis is making a return to the newcastlemax newbuilding market, with his Lavinia Bulkers linked to an order for four vessels worth around $312m in China. Shipbroking sources have identified Zhoushan Changhong International Shipyard as the builder of the 212,000 dwt bulkers, with delivery scheduled for 2030. The reported contract is valued at approximately $78m per vessel and is understood to have been agreed last week. The order would mark Lavinia’s first move into newcastlemax newbuildings since 2013, when the company contracted six ships of this size. Those vessels remain part of the group’s dry bulk fleet. Lavinia has concentrated much of its recent bulker investment on smaller tonnage. The company booked eight kamsarmax newbuildings during 2023 and 2024 at Chinese yards, including CMI, COSCO Heavy Industry and Jiangsu New Hantong. Five have since joined the fleet, with another three scheduled for 2027. The Laskaridis group has also been expanding in crude tankers.In April, its Lavinia Tankers arm was linked to a fourth 157,000 dwt suezmax at South Korea’s DH Shipbuilding, following orders for three sisterships earlier this year. The $89m vessel extended a programme that began with two units in January before the owner exercised additional options.
